# Roadmap

A step-by-step telephone exchange, modelled from first principles in C++23, for no reason.

<!-- Generated by `cairn render`. The items under cairn/items/ are the source;
     this file is a copy, and copies rot. Do not edit it by hand. -->

The project in order, from a battery and two wires to a call between two
machines.

Each milestone is a state the repository can be read in — not a feature set. If
you cloned it at any one of them, the thing would build, run, and make exactly
the claims it had by then earned.

The sequence is deliberate in two respects. **Every check is written before the
apparatus it judges**, and lands expected to fail; the dependencies below
enforce it. And **nothing is judged against a figure nobody can trace**: the
first piece of work in the project is the ledger of published figures, in
`docs/sources.md`, and every check cites it.

The two claims the whole roadmap serves are in `CLAUDE.md` — a phone number is a
set of directions; phreaking has no code — and every item labelled `thesis`
exists to make one of them true or to catch it becoming false. How the team
works the roadmap is in `AGENTS.md`.

    cairn list --view next          what is ready to work on now
    cairn list --view decisions     what only the owner can settle
    cairn list --view thesis        the items the project exists for
    cairn list --view honesty       admissions owed: what is not modelled

## v0.2 — Ten pulses a second

`··········` 0% · 0 of 11 done

A digit is not sent. A finger winds a spring, a governor lets it unwind at ten turns of a cam a second, and the cam breaks the current that many times. At the office, a magnet lifts a shaft one notch per break.

## v0.3 — A number is a set of directions

`··········` 0% · 0 of 21 done

The thesis milestone. A selector climbs to a level and hunts sideways for a free path; a connector climbs to the tens and steps to the units; the line at the end of that path rings. There is no table from numbers to telephones anywhere in the office. A subscriber's number is where their pair is soldered on the frame, and `./laporte spec` reports it as a result.

## v0.4 — Why a telephone sounds like a telephone

`··········` 0% · 0 of 11 done

The battery at the exchange powers your voice. A carbon transmitter is a resistor that a sound wave varies, and the current through it is the telephone signal; with no battery there is no voice at all.

## v0.5 — The network listened on the wire it spoke on

`··········` 0% · 0 of 13 done

A second office, and a trunk between them. An idle trunk carries a 2600 Hz tone; a busy one is silent; dial pulses cross as bursts of tone. The signalling and the voice share one channel.

## v0.6 — Two machines and a socket

`··········` 0% · 0 of 11 done

The trunk crosses a real network. Each of two computers runs an office with a telephone on it — microphone as transmitter diaphragm, speaker as receiver, keyboard as a hand that can do only what a hand can — and the only thing that crosses the network between them is the trunk: eight thousand mu-law bytes a second, each way.
